questions.prompt: What does a horizontal quantum wire represent?

options.text: A qubit's state as it evolves through time
A list of gate names without order
A hardware cable with no mathematical meaning

questions.explanation: A wire tracks a quantum system through the circuit timeline.

questions.prompt: Which operation creates a classical measurement record?
questions.explanation: Measurement converts the quantum state into a classical outcome.
A unitary satisfies U†U=I, which gives an inverse and preserves norm.

questions.prompt: For a circuit that applies H and then Z, what operator product acts on the input?
questions.explanation: Circuit time is H then Z, so the matrix product is ZH with H acting first on the vector.

questions.prompt: What happens to |0> after H then Z?

options.text: It becomes a classical bit immediately

questions.explanation: H creates |+>, then Z changes the relative sign to produce |->.

questions.prompt: Why can H on q0 and H on q1 share one circuit layer?

options.text: They are the same physical operation

questions.explanation: Disjoint operations can be scheduled in parallel under the stated layer convention.

questions.prompt: What is different about applying X conditionally after a measurement?

options.text: A classical result selects the operation instead of a coherent quantum branch
The X matrix stops being unitary

questions.explanation: A measured bit is classical control. It is not a coherent superposition of control outcomes.

questions.prompt: Why cannot a unitary map both |0> and |1> to |0>?

options.text: It would lose input distinctions and have no unitary inverse

questions.explanation: A reversible unitary preserves inner products and cannot collapse two orthogonal inputs into one output.

questions.prompt: Why can a final histogram hide a circuit-order error?

options.text: Different intermediate phases can share a histogram in one basis

questions.explanation: A later basis change may be needed to reveal a phase or ordering difference.

questions.prompt: Which statement about physical cancellation is correct?

options.text: Ideal matrices can cancel while hardware noise remains
Two inverse gates guarantee a perfect device result
Noise makes the ideal algebra invalid

questions.explanation: The ideal model is a baseline; imperfect physical implementations can still add noise.
